entries.name: Alice
entries.look:
Alice is a translucent spirit in a tattered Victorian dress whose anger drives the mansion's pursuit. She recognizes Mario as someone who returned, touches his chest, and appears able to influence or possess him. Alice first appears as a pale figure at the end of a hallway, her form translucent and her eyes green. She speaks in layered voices. Her manner changes when she sees Mario: the hostility softens into a sad, loving smile, and she says, 'You came back.'

entries.name: Boundy
entries.look: Boundy is a conversational Mazebound who intercepted Remi and Markop on the road back to Tymnas's cottage, introduced herself with unsettling cheer, and offered Remi a green apple grown at the hanging tree with what Remi called fresh fertilizer. She relayed a message for Markop — “prepare for consequences” — said goodbye to Remi by name, and departed before Remi realized she had never introduced herself. entries.name: Director Vale
entries.look:
Director Vale appeared after DGK Central denied sending Liam to collect Spirit Residue. He carried a silver Directorate badge, took Liam's phone, and declared the operation under his command despite Central Command's objection. Vale arrives from the bushes while Liam is speaking to DGK Central. His black coat, silver badge, calm voice, and claimed Clearance Level 5 make him look official; his timing and conduct make the claim dangerous. He says he called Liam to the mansion, confiscates the phone, and orders Central Command to stand down.

A vial of Spirit Residue is thrown at Vale and release

entries.name: Dracule Mihawk
entries.look: Dracule Mihawk, known as the Hawk of Blackfen Pass, is a legendary swordsman and silent observer of the Old World's many crises. He stands as a pillar of stoic power, his golden eye glinting with the intensity of frozen fire. He reluctantly agreed to accompany a lone Iron Legion agent into the heart of Mount Ebott after recognizing the sigil of a division that was supposedly wiped out nearly a century ago. entries.name: Earl Grey
entries.look: Earl Grey was the primary enforcer for the Tea Leaf Syndicate—a skilled fighter whose loyalty to Green T was matched only by his combat effectiveness. His death during the Syndicate Showdown was the single most dramatic exit Waluigi has ever witnessed: Roger's poisoned dagger interacted with something in Earl Grey's biology, and the man DETONATED. Waluigi's favorite hat was in the blast radius. Waluigi is still upset about the hat. Earl Grey was the Tea Leaf Syndicate's muscle—the person who handled problems that couldn't be solved with tea and conversation. While Green T maintained the Syndic

entries.name: Elder Rowan Meadowlight
entries.look: Elder Rowan Meadowlight was a respected druid of the Veridian Grove who died on the same day as the Swiftsoul explosion, with Archie Miser found near the scene. The prosecution claims Archie caused his death through reckless magic or deliberate silencing of a witness. The defense evidence suggests the Elder was killed by a sophisticated third party who sabotaged the Grove's ancient wards specifically to frame Archie—the same people responsible for the Swiftsoul explosion. entries.name: Gabriel / Freddy
entries.look:
Gabriel is the child whose spirit was bound to Freddy Fazbear, the lead performer of the original five animatronics at the Hurricane Freddy Fazbear's Pizza — the franchise's crown jewel, and the place where the original five children were murdered. He spent decades on that main stage haunting the night security staff, outlasting the animatronics themselves, until Wario's seven-night tenure ended in the Secret Bunker and thirty years of sustained grief released its hold. The record lists him with two words and no complaints: Released Night Seven. ## The stage

entries.name: John Lee
entries.look: A ceremonial guard at Peach's Castle in the last month of the reign: a Toad whose job was to stand next to a lantern and look like the kingdom was fine. On one night in Efferd, 955 BF he jumped four times because the Mario brothers were coming, got lost five times in the right direction, and ended up in the dungeon corridor where a Koopa who was never locked in shook Fawful's hand with the Mages' Guild watching. He is the only witness the archive has to the Arrangement with a voice, and the first man the Chamberlain told the Guild to kill. He left the castle through the drains with a dead Toad

entries.name: Lady Bloomia
entries.look: Lady Bloomia is the missing link to the greatest conspiracy in the Mushroom Kingdom. She was Princess Peach's handmaiden and the last person to see her alive. She didn't orchestrate the assassination—she smuggled out the evidence, and more importantly, she likely smuggled out Peach's secret half-Rakasha child. She has been running for 85 years, holding the truth in a leather case. Waluigi loves a good scandal, but the 'Bloomia Hypothesis' is a geopolitical earthquake. entries.name: Liam
entries.look: Liam entered the Dread Mansion believing he had been assigned to collect samples for the DGK. A central contact later denied issuing that mission. Liam survived the mansion's pursuit, helped Luigi escape, recovered a vial of Spirit Residue, and confronted Director Vale and a doppelgänger wearing his face. Liam's account begins with a flashlight, an abandoned mansion, and a mission understood to be official. entries.name: Marilyn
entries.look: The only servant the account of the unlocked cell names. At one in the morning, with a kart broadcast audible through the wall, she sat at the long table of the dining hall beside a small Toad boy with a plate in front of him — Toad Lee, the ceremonial guard John Lee's son — and minded him. John Lee saw them from the doorway and did not stop. By dawn the Mages' Guild had the boy and described it as protection. Marilyn is the last person the record places with him before that. Marilyn is a name, a table and a child. The archive has filed people on less and has never been comfortable doing it.

entries.name: Miles Edgeworth
entries.look: Miles Edgeworth is the prosecutor handling the case against Archie Miser for the Swiftsoul explosion. He has a near-perfect conviction rate, especially in high-profile magic cases, and is expected to pursue maximum sentencing on all counts. Whether he knows the evidence against Archie is fabricated, or whether he genuinely believes he's prosecuting a guilty man, will determine whether he's an obstacle or a potential ally in uncovering the truth. entries.name: Piktor Deldkur the Third
entries.look:
Hjumpik's grandfather. Named in the war room of the Overgrown Manor on the morning of 1 Aethel, 922 BF, to a battered fairy who had just been handed the job of running at a monster: even when his arm was cut off he still wanted to fight. The ordinal is the important part — there is a First and a Second. The archive had a Deldkur before it had a Piktor: the grandson's full name has been on file since the Raventree crisis, and no volume in Waluigi's forty contains the rest of the line. That ends with this filing.

entries.name: Riba
entries.look:
Riba owned the Dread Mansion. Alice loved him and he betrayed her; she died on the property and what she left behind went into the house. He appears in the archive only through Luigi's account and through the diary Alice wrote, and every fact about him is secondhand. Riba is named twice in the Dread Mansion transcript and never appears in it. Luigi's account is the whole record: a woman called Alice loved the man who owned the mansion, the man betrayed her, and she died there carrying it.

What makes him worth an entry is not the betrayal but its persistence. While Alice held Mario, Mario talk

The dragon was paralysed by a sonic weapon within the hour. Robinson and Ignis-Major were both taken to Aegis Command. entries.name: The Captain of the Palace Guard (955 BF)
entries.look: The head of the palace guard in the last month of the reign, known to the archive from one account and one night. entries.name: The Unknown Assassin
entries.look: Someone killed Princess Peach on Highsun 1, 955 BF. That person's identity remains the central mystery of the assassination—the question that eighty-five years of investigation, propaganda, and civil war have failed to answer. The official narrative blamed Bowser, but the evidence is weak and Bowser has denied involvement consistently. Lady Bloomia's testimony claims the killer's identity is recorded in Princess Peach's list—'someone the Princess loved,' in the third column headed 'HELD THE BLADE.'
